entry.title: Your Life Is Not a Competition
entry.summary: Sometimes, all it takes is a few minutes of scrolling. You see someone traveling. Someone getting good grades. Someone starting a business. Someone getting their dream job. Someone looking happy and confident. And suddenly, you start looking at your own life differently. “Why am I…
entry.content:
Sometimes, all it takes is a few minutes of scrolling.

You see someone traveling.

Someone getting good grades.

Someone starting a business.

Someone getting their dream job.

Someone looking happy and confident.

And suddenly, you start looking at your own life differently.

“Why am I not there yet?”

The Comparison Trap

Social media makes it easy to compare.

We see people’s achievements, but we don’t always see their struggles.

We see the finished product, but not the process behind it.

We see their best moments while we’re experiencing our ordinary days.

That’s why comparison can be dangerous.

We end up comparing our real life to someone else’s highlight reel.

And sometimes, we forget to appreciate what God is already doing in our own lives.

God Gave You Your Own Journey

Everyone has a different path.

Some people graduate early.

Others take longer.

Some know exactly what career they want.

Others are still figuring it out.

Some people seem to have everything together.

Others are quietly struggling.

That doesn’t mean one person’s life is more valuable than another’s.

God didn’t create us to copy each other’s lives.

Galatians 6:4 says:

“But let every man prove his own work, and then shall he have rejoicing in himself alone, and not in another.”

Instead of constantly asking, “Am I ahead of them?”

Maybe I should ask:

“Am I growing from where I was before?”

Celebrate Without Comparing

It’s okay to be happy when someone else succeeds.

Someone else’s blessing doesn’t mean God has forgotten you.

Someone else’s achievement doesn’t take away your own potential.

Their chapter is not your chapter.

Their timing is not your timing.

And their journey is not your journey.

You can celebrate them while continuing to work on yourself.

Be Thankful for Small Progress

Maybe your progress doesn’t look impressive right now.

Maybe you’re just trying to pass your subjects.

Maybe you’re learning how to manage your time.

Maybe you’re becoming more responsible.

Maybe you’re slowly becoming closer to God again.

Those things matter too.

Growth isn’t always dramatic.

Sometimes it’s simply realizing that you’re handling something better than you did before.

Sometimes it’s choosing not to give up.

Sometimes it’s getting back up after failing.

And sometimes, it’s trusting God one more time.

Look Up, Not Around

When I spend too much time looking at everyone else, I lose sight of where I’m going.

So I want to learn to look up instead.

Look toward God.

Ask Him for wisdom.

Ask Him for direction.

Ask Him to help me become the person He wants me to be.

James 1:5 says:

“If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God…”

I don’t need to compete with everyone around me.

I just need to faithfully walk the path God has given me.

So if you’re feeling behind today, take a breath.

Put the phone down for a moment.

Look at how far you’ve already come.

Then take the next step.

Your life is not a competition.

You don’t have to outrun everyone else.

You just have to keep walking with God.

entry.title: When God Seems Silent
entry.summary: Have you ever prayed about something again and again, but nothing seems to change? You pray for an answer. You pray for a problem to go away. You pray for something you’ve been waiting for. But days pass. Then weeks. Sometimes, even months. And you…
entry.content:
Have you ever prayed about something again and again, but nothing seems to change?

You pray for an answer.

You pray for a problem to go away.

You pray for something you’ve been waiting for.

But days pass.

Then weeks.

Sometimes, even months.

And you start wondering:

“Is God listening?”

I’ve had moments like that too.

Silence Doesn’t Mean Absence

When we don’t receive the answer we were hoping for, it’s easy to think that God isn’t listening.

But silence doesn’t mean God has left.

There are things God is doing that we cannot see yet.

Isaiah 55:8-9 reminds us:

“For my thoughts are not your thoughts, neither are your ways my ways, saith the LORD.”

God sees things differently than we do.

We see what is happening right now.

God sees the whole picture.

Sometimes the Answer Is “Wait”

Waiting is hard.

Especially when we want an answer immediately.

As college students, we’re used to deadlines and schedules. We want to know when something will happen and what the result will be.

But God doesn’t always work according to our timeline.

Sometimes He says yes.

Sometimes He says no.

And sometimes He says wait.

Waiting doesn’t mean doing nothing.

It can be a season of learning, growing, praying, and trusting.

Psalm 27:14 says:

“Wait on the LORD: be of good courage, and he shall strengthen thine heart: wait, I say, on the LORD.”

What If I Don’t Understand?

There are prayers I still don’t understand the answer to.

There are things I wish had happened differently.

There are moments when I ask God why something had to happen in the first place.

And maybe I won’t always get the explanation I want.

But faith isn’t always about having every answer.

Sometimes, faith is choosing to trust God even when I don’t understand.

I can say:

“Lord, I don’t understand this, but I still trust You.”

That’s not weakness.

That’s faith.

Keep Praying

If you’ve been praying for something for a long time, don’t give up just because you haven’t seen an answer yet.

Keep talking to God.

Tell Him what you’re afraid of.

Tell Him what you’re hoping for.

Tell Him when you’re disappointed.

Prayer doesn’t require perfect words.

God already knows what’s in our hearts.

And while we’re waiting for an answer, we can ask Him to help us become stronger, wiser, and closer to Him.

Maybe the Waiting Is Part of the Journey

Looking back, some of the things I desperately wanted didn’t happen the way I expected.

At the time, I didn’t understand why.

But sometimes, what felt like a closed door became a different direction.

What felt like a delay became a lesson.

What felt like silence became a season where I learned to trust God more.

I still don’t understand everything.

And that’s okay.

I don’t need to know everything to keep walking.

I just need to trust the One who does.

“Trust in him at all times; ye people, pour out your heart before him: God is a refuge for us.” — Psalm 62:8

If you’re waiting for an answer today, keep praying.

Keep trusting.

Keep walking.

God is not limited by the silence you can hear.

entry.title: Finding Time for God in a Busy College Life
entry.summary: College can get really busy. There are assignments to finish, projects to work on, exams to study for, and responsibilities that seem to keep coming. Sometimes, my schedule gets so full that I realize I’ve gone through the whole day without spending time with God.
entry.content:
College can get really busy.

There are assignments to finish, projects to work on, exams to study for, and responsibilities that seem to keep coming.

Sometimes, my schedule gets so full that I realize I’ve gone through the whole day without spending time with God.

I tell myself, “I’ll pray later.”

Then later becomes tomorrow.

And tomorrow becomes another day.

Before I know it, I’ve already been putting God at the bottom of my list.

When Life Gets Busy

I think one of the hardest things about college is learning how to manage everything.

We make time for school.

We make time for friends.

We make time for social media.

We make time for the things we enjoy.

But sometimes, we struggle to make time for the One who gave us another day in the first place.

It’s not always because we don’t care about God.

Sometimes, we’re simply distracted.

Sometimes, we’re tired.

Sometimes, we think we need to finish everything else first.

But God shouldn’t only be part of our schedule when we have free time.

It Doesn’t Have to Be Complicated

Spending time with God doesn’t always have to mean having a long Bible study or spending an hour in prayer.

Sometimes, it can start with something simple.

A short prayer before class.

Reading a few verses before going to sleep.

Thanking God for something good that happened during the day.

Asking for wisdom before making a decision.

Taking a few minutes to be quiet and remember that God is with us.

Small moments can become meaningful when we consistently give them to God.

Psalm 119:105 says:

“Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path.”

I don’t need to know the whole path.

I just need enough light for the next step.

Put God First

Matthew 6:33 says:

“But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.”

Putting God first doesn’t mean ignoring school or responsibilities.

It means remembering who comes first in my life while doing those things.

I can study hard and still pray.

I can work toward my goals and still trust God.

I can enjoy college life while remembering that my identity isn’t based on my grades, achievements, or what other people think about me.

Start Again

Maybe you’ve also been distant from God lately.

Maybe you haven’t opened your Bible in weeks.

Maybe your prayer life isn’t what it used to be.

Don’t let guilt convince you that you can’t start again.

Just start.

Open your Bible.

Talk to God.

Even if the prayer is short.

Even if you don’t know what to say.

Come as you are.

There’s no need to wait until your life is perfectly organized before you make room for God.

Start with today.

One verse.

One prayer.

One quiet moment.

Then do it again tomorrow.

College may be busy, but I don’t want to become so busy building my future that I forget the God who holds my future.

“Commit thy works unto the LORD, and thy thoughts shall be established.” — Proverbs 16:3

So today, before I rush into everything else, I want to remember Him first.

entry.title: When You Feel Like You’re Falling Behind
entry.summary: Have you ever looked at someone else’s life and suddenly felt like you’re not doing enough? Maybe they have better grades. Maybe they already know what they want to do after college. Maybe they seem more confident, more successful, or simply more prepared than you.
entry.content:
Have you ever looked at someone else’s life and suddenly felt like you’re not doing enough?

Maybe they have better grades. Maybe they already know what they want to do after college. Maybe they seem more confident, more successful, or simply more prepared than you.

And then you start asking yourself:

“Am I falling behind?”

I’ve asked myself that question too.

Everyone Has Their Own Pace

College can sometimes feel like a race.

We see other people achieving things, graduating, getting jobs, building their careers, and reaching goals. It’s easy to compare our progress with theirs.

But the truth is, we don’t all start at the same place.

We don’t have the same struggles, opportunities, responsibilities, or circumstances.

So maybe I don’t need to measure my journey using someone else’s timeline.

God doesn’t ask me to become someone else.

He asks me to faithfully walk with Him where I am.

God Is Not Finished With Me

There are days when I feel like I should be doing more.

I should be studying harder.

I should be more productive.

I should already know what I’m going to do with my future.

But sometimes, I forget that growth takes time.

Philippians 1:6 says:

“Being confident of this very thing, that he which hath begun a good work in you will perform it until the day of Jesus Christ.”

God is still working.

Even when I don’t see progress.

Even when I make mistakes.

Even when I feel like I’m going backwards.

My current situation isn’t the end of my story.

Don’t Give Up Because You’re Not There Yet

Maybe you’re also in a season where you feel stuck.

Maybe your grades aren’t where you want them to be.

Maybe you’re struggling to stay motivated.

Maybe you’re unsure about your future.

Or maybe you’re simply tired.

It’s okay to admit that.

Being tired doesn’t mean you’re failing.

Taking a little longer doesn’t mean you’re losing.

And not having everything figured out doesn’t mean you’re behind.

Sometimes, progress looks very small.

Getting out of bed and trying again.

Finishing one assignment.

Praying even when you don’t feel like praying.

Opening your Bible after being away from it for a while.

Choosing to keep going.

Those small steps matter.

Keep Walking

I don’t know what your journey looks like right now.

But if you’re feeling behind, remember this:

You don’t have to finish everything today.

Just take the next step.

Trust God with the things you cannot control, and be faithful with what He has placed in front of you today.

Your journey is still being written.

So don’t give up just because you’re not where you want to be yet.

Keep walking.

God isn’t finished with you.

“For a just man falleth seven times, and riseth up again.” — Proverbs 24:16

Maybe you’re not behind.

Maybe you’re simply still on your way.

entry.title: Starting Where I Am
entry.summary: College is a new chapter. It can be exciting, but it can also be confusing. There are days when I feel motivated and ready to do everything, and there are also days when I feel tired, lost, or unsure of what I am doing. Sometimes,…
entry.content:
College is a new chapter.

It can be exciting, but it can also be confusing. There are days when I feel motivated and ready to do everything, and there are also days when I feel tired, lost, or unsure of what I am doing.

Sometimes, I think I need to have everything figured out. I need to know where my life is going, what career I want, and what kind of person I want to become.

But maybe I don't have to know everything yet.

Maybe I just need to take the next step.

Walking With God

One thing I am learning in this season is that I don't have to walk through college alone.

There are many things I cannot control. I don't know what will happen next year, where my choices will lead me, or what challenges I will face. But I know that God is already there.

Proverbs 3:5-6 says:

“Trust in the LORD with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding. In all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths.”

Sometimes trusting God is easier to say than to do.

There are moments when I worry about my future or compare myself with other people. I see people who seem to be ahead of me, and I wonder if I am doing enough.

But God reminds me that my journey does not have to look like someone else's.

College Is More Than Grades

Of course, school is important. There are assignments, projects, exams, deadlines, and sometimes sleepless nights.

But I believe college is also a time to grow as a person.

I am learning how to be responsible, how to handle pressure, how to deal with failure, and how to keep going even when things don't go according to plan.

Some lessons don't come from the classroom.

They come from difficult days.

They come from mistakes.

They come from waiting.

And sometimes, they come from simply choosing to trust God again.

One Step at a Time

I don't know exactly where this journey will take me.

And honestly, I don't think I need to know everything right now.

For now, I want to learn, grow, serve God, and become the person He wants me to be.

This blog is a small part of that journey.

I want to share the things I learn along the way—the struggles, little victories, thoughts, Bible lessons, college experiences, and moments when I see God's goodness in ordinary days.

Maybe someday, I'll look back at these posts and see how much I have changed.

For now, I'm simply starting where I am.

One day.

One lesson.

One prayer.

One step at a time.

“This is the day which the LORD hath made; we will rejoice and be glad in it.” — Psalm 118:24

Welcome to College Days With God.

Let's walk this path together.
